review_notes: I read the whole file and the uses of its simp-relevant lemmas across the repository. I also read liftedGradient_eq_vectorOfLinear in MetricTransport. Only one finding is well supported. liftedGradient_component is the canonical component-expansion lemma. Three files call it through simp/simp_rw, and none of them can rely on default simp. fieldDerivative_linear needs a smoothness hypothesis, so it is not a simp candidate. scalarEmbedding_inner and vector_curlTest_inner are used with rw or simp only in one place each, so I do not recommend simp annotations for them. I did not run Lean. I did not check for conflicting simp lemmas on liftedGradient elsewhere beyond the greps, and I saw none. I also did not check whether coordinateDirection or fieldDerivative are unfolded by other simp sets.

findings.excerpt: liftedGradient period κ m φ x i = fieldDerivative period (coordinateDirection κ m i) φ x
findings.problem: This is the canonical normal form for a component of the lifted gradient: it turns the opaque `liftedGradient … x i` into the primitive `fieldDerivative` along a coordinate direction. It has no simp attribute. Every consumer that wants this normal form passes it by hand to `simp only` or `simp_rw`. That happens here in test_gradient_curl_integral and in ClassicalDivergence and CylinderClassicalSolenoidal. The only other route to a component is the lower-level `liftedGradient_eq_vectorOfLinear`, which exposes `vectorOfLinear` and `fderiv`. So the intended orientation is not encoded in the simp set. The rewrite is terminating, and the right-hand side contains no `liftedGradient`. There is no competing simp rule for this expression in the sources I grepped.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`: `@[simp] theorem liftedGradient_component …`. Call sites could then use plain `simp`, or drop the explicit lemma from `simp only`/`simp_rw` where the default set is acceptable. The orientation stays the same, with `liftedGradient` on the left and `fieldDerivative` on the right. If the author does not want it in the global simp set, a local simp set would also work. It would be named for the lifted-gradient component normal form and used by these three proofs.
findings.benefit: Component expressions of lifted gradients would normalise to `fieldDerivative` along `coordinateDirection κ m i` without each proof having to name the lemma. This is the form that the integration-by-parts and commutation lemmas (`scalar_integration_by_parts`, `fieldDerivatives_commute`) consume. It would also remove the repeated manual `simp_rw [liftedGradient_component]` steps downstream.

evidence.excerpt: vectorOfLinear κ m (fderiv ℝ (localLift period φ x) 0)
